description: Shared Renovate preset for Caracal Lynx repos. Consumers extend it with: "extends": ["local>caracal-lynx/.github:renovate-config"]

hostRules (DAG-3xx, 2026-08-20): npm read auth for the private @caracal-lynx scope. npm answers 404 — NOT 403 — for a restricted package you are not authorised to see, so an unauthenticated Renovate cannot tell 'private' from 'unpublished'. It logs 'no-result' and drops the dependency. The failure is silent: no PR, no error, no failing check, just a collapsed 'Package lookup failures' warning at the bottom of the Dependency Dashboard. Verified 2026-08-20: unauthenticated GET registry.npmjs.org returns 200 for @caracal-lynx/sluice (public) and 404 for @caracal-lynx/sluice-enrich and @caracal-lynx/eslint-config (restricted). sluice resolving is what disguised this — one public package in the scope made the pipeline look healthy.

What it actually broke: sluice-client-eribe last got a Renovate-proposed @caracal-lynx update in #75 (2026-07-16). #95 (~2026-08-03) was opened and then AUTOCLOSED — Renovate withdrawing a PR it could no longer substantiate. Every @caracal-lynx change in that repo since has been made by hand (#92, #102). The trigger was the monorepo cutover: the standalone repos were archived 2026-07-30 and publishing moved to OIDC from data-gubbins, which publishes restricted by default. @caracal-lynx/sluice is deliberately public (open-source; confirmed 2026-08-20) — the other three are deliberately private, and that asymmetry is now load-bearing rather than accidental.

Why this mattered more than staleness: the packages were never actually frozen. lockFileMaintenance regenerates via an authenticated `pnpm install` in CI, so it resolves private packages fine — eribe#98 silently carried eslint-config 0.1.0->0.1.2 and sluice-enrich 1.3.2->1.3.4 under a PR titled only 'chore(deps): lock file maintenance', with lockFileMaintenance.automerge true. So the private first-party packages inverted their own governance: eribe's config says @caracal-lynx/* never auto-merges in client repos and that sluice-enrich 'runs against client data', yet both were updated unreviewed through the one path that does not consult packageRules at all. Same OFFERS-vs-RESOLVES split as the read-excel-file hold (MOI-10 / DAG-301), pointed the other way — there a hold governing offers could not stop a resolution; here review rules governing offers could not review one.

Mechanics: the token VALUE is not in this file and must not be. Mend no longer accepts encrypted secrets in repo config; the credential lives in the Mend portal (developer.mend.io) under Credentials at ORGANISATION scope, named NPM_READ_TOKEN, and is inherited by every repo in the org. This file carries only the reference. Hoisted here rather than into each repo for the same reason as the typescript <7 hold: no repo can miss it, and every future client repo is covered on day one instead of hitting this silently. data-gubbins is unaffected either way — its internal deps are all `workspace:`, which Renovate never looks up.

KNOWN RESIDUAL RISK — read before rotating: if NPM_READ_TOKEN expires or is revoked, this reverts to the exact silent 404 above with no alarm. Prefer a granular read-only token scoped to @caracal-lynx with no expiry; if an expiry is set, the rotation date must be tracked outside npm because nothing here will tell you.

schedule: before 9am on the first day of the month
lockFileMaintenance.description: MOI-3 (DAG-294): monthly, was twice weekly. Lockfile maintenance regenerates the whole tree from manifest ranges, which is how read-excel-file 9.3.8 landed in data-gubbins straight past a Renovate `<9.3.5` hold — a hold binds only if the declared manifest range already excludes the ceiling, and full regeneration re-resolves from the manifest. Twice-weekly full-tree regeneration against a hand-maintained overrides block is churn with a known failure mode: renovate/lock-file-maintenance was the single worst branch in data-gubbins at 23 CI runs. Monthly still prunes stale transitive resolutions and still reconciles the overrides block. Not disabled — that is the only mechanism which does either.

packageRules.description: Fleet-wide hold on v6. Block all of TypeScript 7 (native compiler), open-ended — no auto-resume at 7.1. Decision 2026-07-10; lift this pin manually when we choose to adopt a 7.x line. Hoisted from per-repo renovate.json into the shared preset (DAG) so no repo can miss it (sluice-client-eribe drift, 2026-07-24).

peerDependencies: widen ranges instead of bumping the floor — the global rangeStrategy 'bump' would narrow the supported range (e.g. typescript >=5.9.3 → >=6.0.3), breaking consumers for no benefit (eslint-config#22, 2026-07-16)
Group all @types/* updates together; auto-merge non-major
Group GitHub Actions updates; auto-merge non-major
Group internal @caracal-lynx/* packages — automerge decision left to per-repo overrides
Major bumps always get their own PR and require manual review
Runtime dependencies (anything that ships to users) never auto-merge — manual review enforced

MOI-1 (DAG-292): group pnpm catalog updates into one PR. Catalog entries carry depType 'pnpm.catalog.<name>' — verified as literally 'pnpm.catalog.default' from Renovate 44.30.3 extraction output, 21 of 21 entries, DAG-291. That matches NEITHER the devDependencies nor the dependencies rule above, so before this rule every catalogued dependency got its own PR: adopting the pnpm catalog silently disabled the fleet's main batching rule. On a shared lockfile under strict status checks N separate PRs cost O(N^2) CI runs — 18 PRs produced 983 workflow runs on 2026-08-11. Majors are excluded and keep individual review. automerge is FALSE, deliberately and against the original draft: the catalog mixes dev tooling with nine runtime dependencies that ship to users (commander, pino, pino-pretty, picocolors, csv-stringify, axios, axios-retry, pg, yaml), and because their depType is the catalog one, the runtime-dependency rule above cannot see them — automerge:true here would have reversed the standing no-auto-merge-for-runtime decision by a side door. Placed LAST on purpose: last match wins per field, which also means catalogued @types/* join this group instead of 'type definitions'. That is accepted — it is one fewer PR, and the group needs a human merge either way.

MOI-2 (DAG-293): group runtime dependency patch/minor updates. The rule above sets automerge:false for dependencies and nothing else, so runtime bumps fell through every grouping rule and each opened its own PR — four of the eighteen in the 2026-08-11 wave. automerge stays false: runtime dependencies ship to users and keep manual review. Majors are excluded; a grouped major that fails is genuinely hard to bisect, and majors are where the review value is.
